newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to approve mine contracts but not Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to approve mine contracts but not Busang.

text.p: Indonesia will exclude two applications for contracts of work submitted by Canadian mining company Bre-X Minerals Ltd in a group to be approved later this month, local newspapers reported on Monday.

Simon Sembiring, head of the sub-directorate of mining development, was quoted by Kompas newspaper as saying Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana planned to approve 68 contracts of work by the end of this month.
He said the Bre-X applications for the southeast and northwest zones of the Busang property had been put on hold.

The contracts are crucial for the further exploration and development of the Busang property, which has been in the limelight since Bre-X declared it held 70.95 million ounces of gold and later admitted the estimate might have been overstated.

A ministry official contacted by Reuters declined to comment on Sembiring's remarks, referring questions to the ministry's director-general Adjat Sudradjat. An official at Sudradjat's office said he was attending a meeting.

Bre-X has hired Canadian mining consultant Strathcona Mineral Services to carry out an independent audit on the Busang site to determine the amount of gold in the property. The results are expected in early May.
The Kompas newspaper said President Suharto had given the go-ahead to the 68 so-called sixth generation contracts of work, which had been long delayed due to developments in the Busang saga.
Sembiring said 176 applications for seventh generation contracts of work had been given preliminary approval by Sudjana. He declined to say when they would be forwarded to parliament.
The Jakarta Post said most of the applications were for gold mining projects, and applicants included Barrick Gold Corp and Placer Dome Inc of Canada.

Sembiring said the seventh generation contracts of work would restrict the area to be explored and exploited to 62,500 hectares (154,400 acres) per concession, compared with the current 250,000 hectares.

"While in the previous COW the government had stressed on efforts to raise government revenue through taxes and royalties, the seventh generation COW will emphasise on the aspect of supervision and limitation of areas," he was quoted as saying by the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper.
He said the seventh generation contracts would also tighten supervision of programmes to be carried out by the investors.
"This shows the seriousness of the government regarding mining investors who are going to invest in Indonesia," Sembiring was quoted as saying.
He said when calculations were not rational or programmes could not be completed on schedule, the government had the right to cancel the investor's plan.
The Indonesian government has a 10-percent stake in the Busang property, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc 15 percent, Bre-X 45-percent and Indonesian companies the rest.
